title: HKMA Announces New Phase of Project Ensemble for Tokenised Deposits and Digital Assets
summary: On 13 November 2025, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) published a press release, at the cited URL, whose title -- as identified by that citation -- describes a new phase of Project Ensemble, HKMA's ongoing initiative piloting tokenisation and settlement infrastructure for Hong Kong's financial markets, as supporting 'real-value transactions in tokenised deposits and digital assets.' A tokenised deposit is a bank deposit represented as a transferable digital token rather than only as an entry in a bank's internal ledger. HKMA's press-release page returned no retrievable content on repeated attempts, both when this card was drafted and during independent re-verification, which also could not retrieve the page's RSS listing or other HKMA pages tried as alternates. As a result, the quoted title itself could not be independently authenticated against retrievable source text, and which institutions are participating, the new phase's specific scope, and any stated timeline all remain unconfirmed.
why_it_matters: Project Ensemble is how HKMA tests new settlement infrastructure for tokenised money before it reaches the broader market, so a new phase signals continued development of the initiative. For a newcomer, it shows Hong Kong's central-banking-style regulator actively building infrastructure for tokenised finance, alongside its separate licensing regimes for stablecoins and exchanges.
